scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. The other side sends your client an unsigned copy of an arbitral award. Does the time to challenge it start running?
On twenty sixth October, twenty twenty six, the Kerala High Court, through a single bench of Honourable Justice Mohammed Nias C P, answered that question.
scenes.shown: On 26 October 2026, the Kerala High Court, through a single bench of Honourable Justice Mohammed Nias C.P., answered that question.

scenes.dialogue: An arbitrator passed an award on twenty sixth March, twenty twenty four. The losing party challenged it before the Kottayam court under Section Thirty Four.
scenes.shown: An arbitrator passed an award on 26 March 2024. The losing party challenged it before the Kottayam court under Section 34.

scenes.dialogue: On eighth April, he received an unsigned copy, posted by the award holder's lawyer. The signed copy came from the arbitrator only on twenty third June.
scenes.shown: On 8 April, he received an unsigned copy, posted by the award holder's lawyer. The signed copy came from the arbitrator only on 23 June.

scenes.dialogue: The award holder said the challenge was late: time ran from April, as the other side knew the award's contents. The Kottayam court disagreed, so he came to the High Court.
The question: under Section Thirty Four, sub section Three, does the three month limit run from that unsigned copy, or only from receipt of the signed award?
scenes.shown: The question: under Section 34(3), does the three-month limit run from that unsigned copy, or only from receipt of the signed award?

scenes.dialogue: The High Court held: Section Thirty One needs a signed award, and a signed copy delivered to each party. Mere knowledge of its contents does not start limitation.
scenes.shown: The High Court held: Section 31 needs a signed award, and a signed copy delivered to each party. Mere knowledge of its contents does not start limitation.

scenes.dialogue: Following Supreme Court rulings like Tecco Trichy and Ark Builders, it held: a copy from the opposite party starts no clock, under Section Thirty Four or Thirty Three.
scenes.shown: Following Supreme Court rulings like Tecco Trichy and Ark Builders, it held: a copy from the opposite party starts no clock, under Section 34 or 33.

scenes.dialogue: So time ran from twenty third June, and the challenge was in time. The award holder's petition was dismissed. Advocates, count from receipt of the signed award.
scenes.shown: So time ran from 23 June, and the challenge was in time. The award holder's petition was dismissed. Advocates, count from receipt of the signed award.
